report_title: Final commitment: exact projection and mixed-integer strengthening
claim_class: Exact projection plus mixed-integer strengthening: 3 free objective auxiliaries and their 3 defining equalities eliminated, 210 coefficients tightened (28 activation -4500 -> -4459, 182 resource -25000 -> sum of implied bounds), 16 rounded cycle inequalities added; delivered as forward and reverse integer affine bijections plus a target-LP inclusion with a FiberStrictness point.
claims: 3 claims (cases/test19/preparation.json counts.claims=3): forward integer bijection source->target (7,119 checks, inverse:1), reverse integer bijection target->source (7,103 checks, inverse:0), reverse LP inclusion with both integer modes off (5,109 checks, inverse null); all three carry objective=Equal over the same 1,459-pair projection.

Claim fields are only reverse, input_integers, output_integers, objective, projection, inverse: request.json has no field for the 226 strengthened or added target rows, so the extension is bound purely by being target rows plus the proof blocks that derive them.

1 point: {FiberStrictness:{inclusion_claim:2}} with 1,462 rational source values in LP mode; its refutation is one Lin step (RowLower of CYC0001 plus the 14 observation RowEq facts, constant 0) ending in Absurd, i.e. 673/900 = 2 - 1127/900 > 0, proving the pinned target fiber empty.

Block 0 (740 root steps) proves all 1,668 target rows: unchanged rows are reused source facts or 'Exact', the 210 tightened rows are integer Cases, the 16 added rows are Round facts; blocks 1-2 (210 steps each) prove the 1,655 source rows from target rows, with R0001-R0003 identically zero after substitution.

5 mutants rejected (cases/test19/preparation.json negative_checks): a continuous case-split premise, the unrounded Le used as the cut, a wrong auxiliary reconstruction, a source witness coordinate zeroed without inventory balance, and the fiber constant canceled to -673/900.
proof_encoding: RPA 6, one JSON document: proof.rpa 749,360 B to proof.rpx 543,175 B; 3 claims, 3 blocks each ending in Return{map,checks}, 1 point; request.json 46,272 B, source.mcm 218,809 B, target.mcm 227,516 B, preparation 0.557 s.

Kernel receipt (cases/test19/preparation.json kernel_runs[3]): status VERIFIED, obligations 19,331, branches 210, linear_terms 10,162, substitution_terms 23,830, point_coefficient_terms 5,158, peak_live_facts 740, work 1,093,258 of the 1e9 budget, execute 0.60 s.

7,303 of the obligations are the literal 'Exact' discharge, measured per block as 2,918 / 2,922 / 1,463 on 7,119 / 7,103 / 5,109 checks; 4,377 of them (= 3 x 1,459) are the projection pairs, one per pair per claim, and the rest are trivially zero map and inverse-identity residuals plus the 3 removed source equalities. Rules used: Lin, Cases and Round only, with no lifts.

The point witness is small (1,462 values plus a 2-step refutation), but its 16 observation rows are addressed as RowEq:1668+i, i being the input coordinate index, i.e. the proof depends on the position of kernel-generated rows.
Negative-check receipts: 5 mutated RPAs assembled and verified INVALID against the original request, each recorded with rpa_sha256 and rpx_sha256 (cases/test19/preparation.json negative_checks).
reformulation: input/model.mps 1,462 vars / 1,655 constraint rows (465 E, 1,190 L) / 5,158 constraint nonzeros / 535 integer-marked / 3 FR bounds becomes output/reformulated.mps 1,459 vars / 1,668 rows (462 E, 1,190 L, 16 G) / 4,620 constraint nonzeros and 5,617 including the objective; solver outcome Optimum 988585.62 unchanged; NAME test19 -> RFtest19. Edits: (1) remove R0001-R0003 and free columns C0925-C0927, substituting the objective to 997 terms with constant 0; (2) 28 activation coefficients -4500 -> -4459 on the two cycles with demand 4459; (3) 182 resource coefficients -25000 -> B in {4459, 4500, 8959, 9000, 13500, 18000}, 14 rows keep 25000; (4) add CYC0001-CYC0016 with sum(y) >= ceil(D/M) and RHS 2,2,5,5,4,4,4,4,8,8,2,2,12,12,1,1; (5) every retained name, coefficient, bound record and integer marker unchanged. The projection is exact (feasible assignments and objective values preserved); the strengthening holds only for integer points, and 226 target rows are violated by the source LP witness.
agent_manual_work: Custom exact MPS parser with fractions.Fraction for every coefficient, RHS and bound, plus a second independently written fixed-field parser; both agree on the original (digest eval 'Parsing exact model representation'; digest report section 'Parsing and interpretation').

Hand-built structure mining: incidence analysis of the 462 equality rows of the form s_next - s_current - x = -d, giving 16 disjoint directed cycles (six of 14, four of 28, two of 21, two of 42, two of 70) that telescope to sum(x) = D; 70 packing rows covering 266 binaries; 196 resource rows over 14 integer columns with support sizes 1, 2, 3, 4, 10; a single 1,400-variable component plus 59 isolated objective-only integer columns.

Certificate-grade derivations computed by hand: U_x = min(4500, D) for all 462 production variables with a row pair per variable, B = sum of U_x per resource row (182 below 25000), ceil(D/M) per cycle, and the rational relaxation witness verified by exhaustive arithmetic to satisfy every original bound and row while violating all 16 cycle rows and all 210 tightened rows.

Hypotheses recorded with negative outcomes: no duplicate rows, no optimality-only reduction (the 59 identical objective-only integer columns were retained), no full cycle decomposition, production costs constant only on the two D=4459 cycles.

A 214 KB audit.json as machine-readable edit manifest: removed_rows, removed_columns, coefficient_changes (210 records with row, column, old, new, type, production, cycle), cycle_certificates (16 with rows, production, inventory, activation and D, M, new RHS), production_bound_certificates (462), resource_bound_certificates (196), original_relaxation_witness (1,462 values).

evaluate (tools/prepare_test71.py:16-29) is a Python oracle over bounds, rows and the objective; the preparer asserts 0 source violations, exactly 226 target violations and equal objective values (tools/prepare_test19.py:117-119).
friction: No public proof-construction API: the 19,331 obligations and all 226 rule applications are hand-written dict literals; the only constructors are test-local (crates/core/tests/flow_builder.rs and its siblings cover lifts only, and crates/core/src/build_support.rs exposes no public function).

The preparer's ground truth is an untrusted 214 KB audit.json plus two MPS files: every record is re-derived and re-asserted inline (tools/prepare_test19.py:33-46, 47-52, 74), and any disagreement between the agent's parser and rpx canonical would surface only as a failed kernel run.

Projection redundancy: the same 1,459 identity pairs are written three times (45,876 of request.json's 46,272 B) and must be discharged as 4,377 'Exact' checks; there is no way to say 'the identity part of this claim's Return map'.

The fiber refutation references kernel-generated observation rows by raw index RowEq:1668+i; the required convention 'observation order equals input coordinate order' exists only as a code comment (tools/prepare_test19.py:121) and a permuted projection list would silently mislead it.

Structural lookups are hand-rolled full scans: the unique activation row of each production variable is found by scanning all 1,655 source rows for an exact 2-term signature (tools/prepare_test19.py:65-68) and the defining equality of each eliminated column by scanning removed_rows (line 36), while cycle rows, inventory partners and activation columns come from the agent's audit file rather than from the canonical model.
extension_binding: Adding rows to the target needs no claim-level declaration: request.json contains only claims and points. (a) In the forward integer claim each of the 16 CYC rows is an ordinary output obligation, discharged by a Round fact built as Lin of the telescoped cycle equalities (over the possibly tightened activation rows) plus Int over the 462 binaries, i.e. sum(y) >= ceil(D/M); the 210 tightened rows are discharged by 2-branch Cases on the same integer column (z <= 0 uses the original row, z >= 1 uses the implied bounds U_x and B). (b) In both reverse claims the added rows are input premises, so the extension creates zero reverse obligations; the 3 removed source equalities instead fall out as 'Exact' because the reverse map is the substitution derived from them, and the 210 tightened rows are weakened back with one Lin each using nonnegativity of the tightened column. (c) Strictness is not declared per row either: the FiberStrictness point proves the pinned target fiber empty using only CYC0001 and its 14 coordinates, margin 673/900.
strictness_binding: Version 6, so V6 FiberStrictness with a complete coordinate projection, not V10. The point payload is one 1,462-value source LP point (checked LP-feasible) plus a fresh-scope refutation of the whole pinned target LP; the pinned coordinates are the claim's complete 1,459-pair projection, appended as observation rows in request order (docs/FIBER_POINT_V6.md:9-13, 38-40). No V10 feature was needed: there is no objective-level claim and no input halfspace (cases/test19/README.md:19-20), and V10 ImageExclusion alone would prove less, being one separating image rather than strict inclusion (docs/FORMAT_V10_DRAFT.md:118). The bijection is bound by the legacy Claim.inverse pair (1 and 0), not by a V7 BijectionWitness.

notes: Scale: 1,462/1,459 vars, 1,655/1,668 rows, 5,158/4,620 constraint nonzeros; RPA 749,360 B (0.3% of the 256 MiB text limit), RPX 543,175 B, request.json 46,272 B; verification is cheap (work 1,093,258 of 1e9, 0.69 s total), so no need here is driven by budget pressure or the 256 MiB ceiling. The reformulation is certification-motivated: the solver outcome is unchanged (Optimal 988585.62 both ways) and no objective improvement is claimed, so performance is not the reason for any need. Corpus shape: growing the target is rare but not unique (test49, test66, test71 also add rows); what is distinctive here is adding 16 rows while tightening 210 coefficients in place and eliminating 3 free columns, so one edit list drives three different obligation shapes and the compiler must classify each edit by direction and integrality. Siblings sharing the 3-claim bijection pattern: test17; siblings whose certificate is a per-record edit expansion: test17, test12.
